title: Viva Engage: apply Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels to communities
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, licensing quotations and configuration controls are supported by Microsoft documentation. Minor corrections should complete the guest-access path, acknowledge conflicting guidance about updating labels already applied to groups, and identify checklist controls missing from the table.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationales
claims.claim: A community's label can set its public or private privacy setting.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Sensitivity labels control whether guests can be added to Engage communities.
claims.quote: Use sensitivity labels to control guest access to your communities. Communities created with a label that doesn’t allow guest access are only available to users in your organization.

claims.claim: Labels can be applied to communities after labels and their policies are configured in Purview.
claims.quote: After you configure sensitivity labels with their associated policies in the Microsoft Purview portal, these labels can be applied to communities in your organization.

claims.claim: The configured default sensitivity label automatically applies when a user creates a community.
claims.quote: Admins can set up sensitivity labels to automatically apply during community creation. When a user creates a new community, the default sensitivity label automatically applies to the community.

claims.claim: Community creators can choose a different label from the labels available to them.
claims.quote: The user can select a different label from the list of available labels, but they can't create new labels.

claims.claim: Community creators cannot create new sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: The user can select a different label from the list of available labels, but they can't create new labels.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Community admins can change a community's sensitivity label and its resulting privacy setting.
claims.quote: Community admins can change the sensitivity label (and hence its privacy setting) of a community.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: A community admin changes its label by opening the community, selecting More > Settings and choosing from the label dropdowns.
claims.quote: Open the community, select the More menu (...), and choose Settings. ... Depending on how the policies are configured, other choices might be available for each of the two dropdowns.

claims.claim: Users see the community's sensitivity label in its banner.
claims.quote: After the community is live, the sensitivity label appears to users in the community banner:

claims.claim: Admins can configure an Engage community default label in Purview label policy settings.
claims.quote: As an example, select a preferred default label for Engage communities in Microsoft Purview as part of label policy settings.

claims.claim: The Engage community default label takes precedence over the default label for sites.
claims.quote: This new default takes precedence over the default label for sites.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; controls[3].governs; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Public or Private label settings replace and lock container privacy until the sensitivity label is removed.
claims.quote: Your chosen setting replaces any previous privacy setting that might be configured for the container, and locks the privacy value so it can be changed only by first removing the sensitivity label from the container.

claims.claim: People outside the organisation cannot be added to a community created with a label that disallows guest access.
claims.quote: Communities created with a label that doesn’t allow guest access are only available to users in your organization. People outside your organization can’t be added to the community.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Enabled and configured container labels can be offered to Engage users, including labels already used for other supported containers.
claims.quote: After you enable and configure sensitivity labels for containers, users can additionally see and apply sensitivity labels to containers that support them. These include Microsoft team sites, Microsoft 365 groups, SharePoint sites, Viva Engage communities, and Loop workspaces.

claims.claim: Label support must be enabled for Microsoft 365 groups before published labels can be applied.
claims.quote: To apply published labels to groups, you must first enable the feature.

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope; controls[1].note; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Execute-AzureAdLabelSync in Security & Compliance PowerShell synchronises labels to Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: You now need to synchronize your sensitivity labels to Microsoft Entra ID. First, connect to Security & Compliance PowerShell. ... Then run the following command ... Execute-AzureAdLabelSync

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Labels need the Groups & sites scope to configure container privacy and external user access settings.
claims.quote: Follow the general instructions to create or edit a sensitivity label and make sure you select Groups & sites for the label's scope:

claims.claim: The Engage documentation describes a more permissive community default alongside a more restrictive SharePoint site default.
claims.quote: Create a more permissive default for Engage communities, while maintaining a more restrictive default for sites.

claims.claim: Public container privacy allows anyone in the organisation to access the labelled container.
claims.quote: Privacy: Keep the default of Public if you want anyone in your organization to access the container where this label is applied.

claims.claim: Items inside labelled containers do not inherit the container label.
claims.quote: Items in these containers however, do not inherit the labels

claims.claim: A container label does not apply content markings or encryption to the content within it.
claims.quote: Items in these containers however, do not inherit the labels and therefore don't apply any item-level label settings, such as content markings and encryption.

claims.where: Risk assessment; controls[4].note; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Changing External users access applies the new setting to new users but does not revoke existing guests' access.
claims.quote: The new setting applies to new users but not to existing users. For example, if this setting was previously selected and as a result, guest users accessed the site, these guest users can still access the site after this setting is cleared in the label configuration.

claims.claim: EnableMIPLabels is a tenant-level Microsoft Entra group setting rather than an Engage-only switch.
claims.quote: Fetch the current group settings for the Microsoft Entra organization and display the current group settings. ... Name = "EnableMIPLabels" ... Value = "True"

claims.claim: Enabling and configuring container labels makes them available for team sites, Microsoft 365 groups, SharePoint sites and Loop workspaces.
claims.quote: After you enable and configure sensitivity labels for containers, users can additionally see and apply sensitivity labels to containers that support them. These include Microsoft team sites, Microsoft 365 groups, SharePoint sites, Viva Engage communities, and Loop workspaces.

claims.claim: The Engage page describes manual label selection and automatic application of a configured default during community creation.
claims.quote: When a user creates a new community, the default sensitivity label automatically applies to the community. The user can select a different label from the list of available labels, but they can't create new labels.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Purview advises waiting at least one hour before testing a new container label without Teams shared channel controls.
claims.quote: New label: Wait at least one hour, unless your configured settings include Teams shared channel controls.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: A new label configured with Teams shared channel controls requires a wait of at least 24 hours before testing.
claims.quote: New label: Wait at least one hour, unless your configured settings include Teams shared channel controls. If that's the case, wait at least 24 hours.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Purview advises waiting at least 24 hours before testing an existing label.
claims.quote: Existing label: Wait at least 24 hours.

claims.claim: Changes to a label already applied to containers take at least 24 hours to replicate.
claims.quote: If you do, remember to wait at least 24 hours for the changes to replicate to all containers that have the label applied.
claims.fix: Add: 'The cited Entra guide gives different guidance for existing Microsoft 365 groups: changes to published label group settings are not automatically applied to labelled groups and require manual reapplication.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/users/groups-assign-sensitivity-labels#group-setting-changes-to-published-labels-arent-updated-on-the-groups.

claims.claim: The same manual-labelling table includes Enterprise Mobility + Security E3/E5.
claims.quote: | Enterprise Mobility + Security E3/E5 | ... | Manual Sensitivity Labeling | Included | Included | Included | Included | Included |

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The same section also says sensitivity labelling, including automatic or policy-based labelling, requires Microsoft 365 E5 or IPG.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labeling, including automatic or policy‑based labeling, requires a Microsoft 365 E5 license or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance (IPG).

claims.claim: Neither of those service-description licensing statements names Engage communities or publishes an Engage-specific entitlement.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Engage communities sensitivity labels licensing requirements default label not configured audit activities. Read the Purview service description's Information Protection sensitivity labeling section and the Engage sensitivity-label page; neither names an Engage-specific licence.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; controls[1].note; rationale: cost
claims.claim: At least one active Microsoft Entra ID P1 licence must exist in the organisation to configure sensitivity labels for groups.
claims.quote: To configure this feature, there must be at least one active Microsoft Entra ID P1 license in your Microsoft Entra organization.

claims.claim: Tenant admins create and publish sensitivity labels in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: Tenant and network admins create and publish sensitivity labels in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Global Administrators or Yammer Administrators (Viva Engage admins) can change the Engage disable-labels switch.
claims.quote: This tenant-level setting can be changed by Microsoft Entra Global Administrator or Microsoft Entra Yammer Administrator (Viva Engage admin).

claims.claim: The Engage page says PowerShell cmdlets do not directly support assigning sensitivity labels to Engage communities.
claims.quote: Before you use sensitivity labels for Engage, PowerShell cmdlets don't directly support sensitivity labels. Users can't directly specify sensitivity labels for Engage communities.

claims.claim: Using PowerShell to label a community's connected SharePoint site updates the community's label as a workaround.
claims.quote: As a workaround, you can use PowerShell to apply labels to a SharePoint site that connects to an existing Engage community. Doing so causes the label on the Engage community to correspondingly update.

claims.claim: The Entra enablement procedure connects to Microsoft Graph with Directory.ReadWrite.All.
claims.quote: Connect-MgGraph -Scopes "Directory.ReadWrite.All"

claims.claim: Set-Label runs in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy runs in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is functional only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: The Engage admin-center route is Tenant settings > Sensitivity label management > Edit > Disable sensitivity labels for communities > Public or Private (or both).
claims.quote: Select Tenant settings. ... Under Sensitivity label management, select Edit to access the Disable sensitivity labels for communities option ... Select Public, Private, or both.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no PowerShell or API equivalent for the Engage tenant's Disable sensitivity labels for communities switch.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Engage "Disable sensitivity labels" API PowerShell Graph; "Viva Engage" "sensitivity" "disable" "API" tenant. Read Engage identity and labelling guides, Graph engagement API overview and beta community resource; no tenant label-disable operation documented.

claims.claim: No admin UI is documented for enabling the Microsoft 365 groups EnableMIPLabels tenant prerequisite.
claims.quote: Searched: "EnableMIPLabels" "admin center" enable sensitivity labels UI. Read Entra groups-assign-sensitivity-labels and Purview sensitivity-labels-teams-groups-sites; enablement uses PowerShell, while documented UI routes assign labels rather than enable tenant support.

claims.claim: Update-MgBetaDirectorySetting -DirectorySettingId $grpUnifiedSetting.Id -BodyParameter $params sets tenant label support with EnableMIPLabels=True in $params.
claims.quote:
Name = "EnableMIPLabels"
Value = "True"
...
Update-MgBetaDirectorySetting -DirectorySettingId $grpUnifiedSetting.Id -BodyParameter $params

claims.claim: The Purview publishing route is Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies > Publish label > Choose sensitivity labels to publish.
claims.quote: Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies. ... select Publish label ... On the Choose sensitivity labels to publish page, select the Choose sensitivity labels to publish link.

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity "<policy name>" -AddLabels "<label>" adds a sensitivity label to the identified policy.
claims.quote: The AddLabels parameter specifies the sensitivity labels that you want to add to the policy. You can use any value that uniquely identifies the label. For example: Name ... GUID

claims.claim: The modern Purview route through Sensitivity labels > + Create > Label > Define the scope for this label > Groups & sites leads to Define protection settings for groups and sites > Privacy and external user access settings > Privacy.
claims.quote: make sure you select Groups & sites for the label's scope ... on the Define protection settings for groups and sites page ... Privacy and external user access settings to configure the Privacy and External users access settings.

claims.claim: Set-Label -Identity "<label>" -SiteAndGroupProtectionPrivacy Private sets the label's container privacy to Private.
claims.quote: The SiteAndGroupProtectionPrivacy parameter specifies the privacy level for the labe. Valid values are: Public; Private.

claims.claim: The guest-access route follows the modern label wizard to Privacy and external user access settings.
claims.quote: If you selected Privacy and external user access settings, now configure the following settings: ... External user access: Control whether the owner can add guests to the container
claims.fix: Complete controls[4].ui.path as 'Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > + Create > Label > Define the scope for this label > Groups & sites > Define protection settings for groups and sites > Privacy and external user access settings > External user access', using https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/sensitivity-labels-teams-groups-sites.

claims.claim: Set-Label -Identity "<label>" -SiteAndGroupProtectionAllowAccessToGuestUsers $false disables guest access through the label.
claims.quote: The SiteAndGroupProtectionAllowAccessToGuestUsers parameter enables or disables access to guest users. Valid values are: $true: Guest access is enabled. $false: Guest access is disabled.

claims.claim: Publishing policy scope determines which users and groups see and can apply labels.
claims.quote: Label without protection: The publishing policy scope determines which users can see and apply the label. ... Label with protection: The publishing policy still determines who can see and apply the label.

claims.claim: Users, groups and Apply this label by default to groups and sites are configured in the label-policy Create policy configuration.
claims.quote: As part of the label policy, you select users and groups ... The policy settings that you see match the scope of the labels that you selected. ... Apply this label by default to groups and sites

claims.claim: Public and Private are valid SiteAndGroupProtectionPrivacy parameter values.
claims.quote: Valid values are: Public; Private

claims.claim: Admins can disable labels for public communities, private communities or both, allowing their creation without a selected sensitivity label.
claims.quote: Viva Engage admins can disable sensitivity labels for public communities, private communities, or both. When sensitivity labels are disabled, users can create communities without selecting a sensitivity label.

claims.claim: Disabling Engage sensitivity labels does not remove existing community labels or their protections.
claims.quote: Disabling sensitivity labels doesn't remove labels already applied to existing communities. Existing labels and their protections remain in place unless the label is changed explicitly.

claims.claim: Purview advises avoiding changes to the site and group settings of sensitivity labels already applied to containers.
claims.quote: As a best practice, don't change the site and group settings for a sensitivity label after the label has been applied to teams, groups, or sites.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The feature is admin-opt-in because container label support must be enabled and labels configured and published before use.
claims.quote: If you haven't yet enabled sensitivity labels for containers, do the following set of steps as a one-time procedure: ... Until sensitivity labels are enabled for containers, the settings are visible but you can't configure them.

claims.claim: Manual sensitivity labelling is included in the product licences named in the notes, with the documented licensing discrepancy retained.
claims.quote: | Manual Sensitivity Labeling | Included | Included | Included | Included | Included |

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout and After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist names community label assignment and removal of existing guests as controls, but neither has a corresponding table row.
claims.quote: to set it they open the community, select More > Settings ... remove existing guests separately ... Table rows cover label disablement, tenant enablement, publishing, privacy and guest admission, not community assignment or membership removal.
claims.fix: Remove the community-setting procedure from the At rollout checklist bullet, retaining 'Tell community admins that changing a community's label changes its privacy.' Replace 'if guest access is tightened, remove existing guests separately' with 'tightening guest access does not revoke existing guests' access'. No additional control rows are requested.

claims.claim: Purview advises removing a container sensitivity label from every publishing policy before deleting it.
claims.quote: Remove the sensitivity label from all label policies that include the label.

claims.claim: Purview advises waiting at least one hour after removing a container label from all publishing policies before deletion.
claims.quote: Remove the sensitivity label from all label policies that include the label. ... Wait at least one hour.

claims.claim: Purview warns that deleting a container label still included in publishing policies can cause creation failures for new teams, groups and sites.
claims.quote: If you delete a sensitivity label that has the site and group settings enabled, and that label is included in one or more label policies, this action can result in creation failures for new teams, groups, and sites.

claims.claim: Purview describes auditing sensitivity-label additions and removals on sites and groups.
claims.quote: When somebody adds or removes a sensitivity label to or from a site or group, these activities are also audited but without automatically generating an email.

claims.claim: Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > + Create > Label > Define the scope for this label is the documented modern label-scheme route.
claims.quote: Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels ... select + Create and then Label to start the new sensitivity label configuration. ... On the Define the scope for this label page
